title: Microwaves Could Make French Fries Way Healthier — And Still Super Crispy!
summary:
Have you ever wondered why french fries taste so good but aren't exactly a health food? It's because they soak up a ton of oil when they're fried. That oil makes them crispy and delicious, but it also adds lots of fat and calories. Now, scientists think they've found a way to fix that — using microwaves!

Researchers at the University of Illinois discovered that frying potatoes with microwave energy can cut down the oil they absorb. Here's the cool part: microwaves heat food from the inside out. When you fry potatoes normally, heat moves from the hot oil into the potato. Water inside the potato turns to steam and escapes, leaving tiny empty spaces. Then, like a straw sucking up a drink, oil gets pulled into those spaces. But microwaves change the game.

Professor Pawan Singh Takhar, who led the study, explains it like this: "Think about a straw in a drink. If you push air into the straw, it creates positive pressure and any liquid will be pushed out. But if you suck on the straw, the liquid moves upward." In a potato, microwaves create more steam inside, which builds up positive pressure. That pressure pushes oil out instead of letting it soak in. So the fries end up less greasy but still crispy.

The team used a special microwave fryer that could work at two different frequencies — 2.45 gigahertz (like your kitchen microwave) and 5.8 gigahertz. They cut potatoes into strips, blanched them (a quick dip in hot water), and fried them in soybean oil at 180 degrees Celsius. By measuring temperature, pressure, and oil content, they saw exactly how microwaves kept oil out. They even used computer models to study the process in detail.

Why does this matter? If this method works in big factories, we could get fries that taste just as good but are much healthier. That means you might enjoy your favorite snack without as much worry. The next step is figuring out how to make this work on a large scale. So, next time you bite into a fry, remember: science might be making it better for you!
why_it_matters: If this microwave frying trick works in factories, the french fries you eat at home or in restaurants could be much healthier, so you can enjoy them more often.

questions.question: Why do french fries usually have a lot of fat?
options: Because they soak up oil when fried
Because they are cooked in water
Because they are made from potatoes
questions.correct_answer: Because they soak up oil when fried

questions.question: How do microwaves heat food differently from normal frying?
What does positive pressure do to oil inside a potato?
What frequencies did the special microwave fryer use?
What is blanching?
options: Frying in oil for a long time
A quick dip in hot water
questions.correct_answer: A quick dip in hot water

questions.question: What do scientists need to figure out next?
options: How to make potatoes without water
How to fry with ice cubes
How to make the method work in big factories
How to make fries taste worse

background_read: People have been frying potatoes for hundreds of years, but too much fat from fried foods can lead to health problems like obesity.
Scientists at the University of Illinois (a large American university) are always looking for ways to make favorite snacks healthier without ruining the taste.
Microwaves were first used to heat food accidentally, when an engineer noticed a candy bar melting in his pocket near radar equipment.
